getting-started/index.title: Start here
getting-started/index.body:
## What this package is

`zudo-scope10` is the ten-input waveform monitor, separated from the five-oscillator instrument. “LED” in the request is interpreted as the LCD/display project. The LED-lamp repository supplies the documentation pattern, not the circuit.

This release is a **pre-layout engineering handoff**. It contains a specified circuit, native schematic drafts, analytical calculations, control/UI prototype, selected component evidence, firmware core tests and manufacturing instructions. It does not contain a completed routed PCB, verified Gerbers, production CPL, completed LCD firmware or an approved order.

## The first hardware build

Use one factory-populated custom carrier, one factory-headered Raspberry Pi Pico H, and one preassembled Waveshare Pico-ResTouch-LCD-3.5 (SKU 19907). Keep ten independent inputs, ten TIME pots and ten three-position RANGE switches. One LCD shows ten panes at once.

No soldering at home is required or assumed. All PCB components, including through-hole controls, connectors and headers, belong on the factory BOM. Modules are plugged into already-soldered connectors with power off. Any needed electrical repair goes to the assembler or a contracted rework service.

## Local sequence

1. Run `python3 scripts/validate.py` from the project root. This checks the data and generated files, not electrical safety.
2. Run `python3 scripts/serve.py`, then browse `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`. The offline catalogue and UI simulation work without npm packages.
3. Read the power/interface gates and the component pin maps before opening `hardware/kicad/zudo-scope10-p0.kicad_pro`.
4. Resolve the display module's power/header revision and the physical jack, switch, socket and cap drawings before finishing footprints or placement.
5. Complete local KiCad review, layout, ERC/DRC and assembly review. Do not order the outline-only `.kicad_pcb`.

The documentation can be read immediately as Markdown. The included `doc/` contains native zudo-doc configuration and MDX content. Use `scripts/bootstrap_doc.sh` to obtain the official scaffold in a new directory when you prefer that route. No repository, online document or order has been modified.

architecture/brief.title: P0 specification and tradeoffs
architecture/brief.body:
## Fixed scope

| Item | P0 proposal |
|---|---|
| Inputs | 10 independent DC-coupled mono signals |
| Viewing | 1 LCD; portrait 320 × 480 logical pixels; 2 columns × 5 rows |
| Controls | 10 TIME pots, 10 three-position RANGE switches, HOLD and LINK buttons |
| Vertical display scales | ±3 V, ±5 V, ±8 V; software changes only |
| Input working target | ±12 V, subject to qualification |
| Power | USB 5 V only; no USB-PD or Eurorack power header |
| Acquisition target | 10,000 samples/second/channel, sequential; not yet implemented or measured |
| Intended useful signal range | CV/LFO and low audio, approximately DC–1 kHz |
| Time windows | 2 ms–8.192 s across the whole pane, not per division |
| Approximate panel envelope | 250 × 180 mm; control placement is only a study |

The 1 kHz intention is not a guaranteed metrology bandwidth. At 10 ksample/s/channel, Nyquist is 5 kHz; a 20 kHz input can alias severely. Two nominal 3.39 kHz RC poles only provide about 10 dB attenuation at Nyquist. The front end is therefore **not a brick-wall anti-alias filter**. Do not claim accurate full-audio-band viewing.

## Why modules for the first carrier

The [Waveshare module](https://www.waveshare.com/Pico-ResTouch-LCD-3.5.htm) documents 480 × 320 pixels, a 5 V supply, an installed female Pico header, a 73.44 × 48.96 mm active area and an 86 × 57.2 mm PCB. Its SPI-to-parallel bridge is part of the module. Buy the exact assembled version.

[Pico H](https://www.raspberrypi.com/products/raspberry-pi-pico/) includes the headers; an ordinary unheadered Pico does not meet the project requirement. The custom carrier uses two female strips for Pico H and separate male strips for the display. Most spare display contacts are deliberately isolated rather than blindly passed through.

This costs more than a bare RP2040 plus a bare display. The prototype exception avoids designing the MCU's USB/flash/regulator board and an insufficiently documented LCD interface at the same time as ten analog inputs. A later revision may integrate both after their performance is established.

## Not selected for P0

HS35B01A / C19632787 remains a cost-down candidate, not the baseline: the public listing does not establish a reviewed serial interface, power arrangement, connector pin map or exact drawing. Do not treat the earlier roughly $9 display figure as the cost of the present module or the finished instrument.

No touchscreen interaction, SD storage, FFT, tuner, signal generator, audio output, battery, network feature or oscillator core is included. TOUCH and SD chip-selects are held inactive. The presence of those parts on the purchased module does not put them in our feature list.

architecture/input-front-end.title: Input circuit and analytical checks
architecture/input-front-end.body:
## Repeated channel

The same circuit is instantiated ten times. A 1 MΩ input resistor feeds a node connected through 200 kΩ to the buffered 3.0 V reference and through 249 kΩ to ground. A 470 pF C0G capacitor makes the first low-pass pole. A unity buffer, 4.7 kΩ / 10 nF C0G low-pass stage and second unity buffer feed the signal multiplexer.

BAV199 provides a low-leakage dual-diode clamp at the biased node. It is **silicon, not a Schottky device**. The node is protected primarily by high series resistance and the documented amplifier input current path; a diode to a rail is not by itself proof that all absolute-maximum conditions are satisfied.

Two complete channels use one physical TLV9064IDR. U1–U5 provide the 20 input buffer amplifiers. U6 supplies the three post-mux buffers and the reference buffer. The design data enumerate every physical IC pin, rather than inventing multiple U references for the same package.

## Transfer function

Let `G = 1/1M + 1/200k + 1/249k`. For an ideal low-impedance source:

```text
Vnode = ((Vin / 1M) + (Vref / 200k)) / G
      = 0.099839615 × Vin + 1.497594226 V, with Vref = 3.0 V
Vin   = (Vnode - 1.497594226) / 0.099839615
```

At −12 V the nominal node is 0.299519 V; at +12 V it is 2.695670 V. Both leave nominal headroom on a 3.3 V analog rail. The 0.1% divider-resistor / 0.15% reference corner enumeration spans 0.294579 V at the negative end to 2.700079 V at the positive end. **This excludes op-amp offset, temperature, diode leakage, source resistance, ADC errors, capacitance tolerance and PCB parasitics.** It is not a complete tolerance certification.

The effective Thevenin resistance is 99.84 kΩ, giving a first pole near 3,392 Hz. The second pole is near 3,386 Hz. Nominal combined attenuation is −0.19 dB at 500 Hz, −0.73 dB at 1 kHz, −2.60 dB at 2 kHz and −10.04 dB at 5 kHz. These filters soften pulse/saw edges, even when their fundamentals are below 1 kHz.

Run `python3 scripts/analyze.py` to reproduce all values. `reports/analog-analysis.json` and `reports/filter-response.csv` are calculated, not measured. `simulation/input-channel.cir` is an ideal-buffer ngspice starting model; vendor macro-model and transient/fault validation have not been run.

## Input loading and open cables

Small-signal input impedance is approximately 1.111 MΩ. The biased resistor network sends approximately 1.50 µA into a source held at 0 V. A 1 kΩ source resistance can therefore create millivolt-scale bias error.

**An unconnected input does not read 0 V.** With the selected unswitched jack open, its biased node settles near 1.663697 V, which is displayed as approximately +1.663697 V after the nominal conversion. This is an expected P0 limitation, not a detected connected signal. The software must never silently subtract every channel's power-up value, because that would erase legitimate DC voltages.

A later switched jack that shorts the input to ground while unplugged can solve this, but it requires a new exact part, pad/contact map and mechanical qualification. The current PJ-313 5JCJ is not a switched/normalled jack.

## Protection is an open engineering gate

±24 V is a **test target**, not a qualified rating. The 1 MΩ resistor bounds an approximate positive injection current to 24 µA/channel. Ten such channels could inject 240 µA into an unpowered system; a 1 kΩ analog-rail bleed gives an ideal 0.24 V bound under that simplified assumption. Negative injection, individual internal rail paths, ESD, latch-up, diode forward voltages, power sequencing and leakage are not proved by that arithmetic.

Before connecting this prototype to valued equipment, qualify positive/negative powered and unpowered inputs with current-limited fixtures at the assembler or bench-service provider. Never connect mains, speakers/amplifier outputs, unknown industrial voltages or a different ground potential. The instrument is non-isolated and its ground may be bonded to a USB computer.

architecture/power-and-module-interface.title: Power and module interface — stop gate
architecture/power-and-module-interface.body:
## One source only

Pico H's USB input supplies `VBUS_USB`. Carrier F1 passes it to `+5V_FUSED` for the display and the analog regulator. There is no external second supply connection. An eventual suitable USB 5 V source and the Pico USB/VBUS path must satisfy the measured total load and inrush. A 1 A-rated charger is a planned source, not permission to draw 1 A through an unverified PCB/header path.

The analog LDO is TLV75533PDBVR: 3.3 V output, input supply constrained to the [manufacturer limits](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tlv755p.pdf). Use the exact DBV pin assignment (1 IN, 2 GND, 3 EN, 4 NC, 5 OUT). EN is tied to fused 5 V. Use effective input/output capacitance of at least 1 µF as required by the datasheet. No PD voltage negotiation is present.

REF3330 generates 3.0 V and U6D buffers it. The ADC still uses Pico's own reference arrangement; two-point calibration is required to relate the separately generated analog bias to the ADC. The 3.0 V node is not incorrectly connected to Pico ADC_VREF.

## USB source contract

The display and analog-rail load on `+5V_FUSED` is unconditional: it is not gated by USB configuration state, suspend, or any firmware action (F1 passes `+5V_FUSED` to the display header and the analog regulator unconditionally). Because that load is not enumeration-gated, this module cannot rely on an ordinary host port's staged USB power budget (100 mA before configuration, 500 mA after). `design/power-contract.json` records the explicit supported-source contract instead: a USB port or supply that delivers **at least 500 mA at 5 V from attach**, independent of USB enumeration/configuration. Presence of 5 V on VBUS (e.g. a GPIO VBUS-sense pin) does not establish this -- it proves only that a 5 V source is attached, not that it can sustain the required current or that any USB configuration has occurred. An earlier draft's GPIO24/VBUS-sense suggestion is removed for exactly that reason (`design/power-contract.json`'s `decision_notes.rejected_gpio24_vbus_sense`).

Before configuration, during suspend, across a reset, and while the RP2040 bootrom is in BOOTSEL mode, this module draws more than the USB 2.0 unconfigured/suspend limits on an ordinary host port. Only a source meeting the contract above is supported in any of those states. The RP2040 bootrom presents its own USB descriptor during BOOTSEL, including its own declared max-power value; that value comes from the bootrom, not this project's firmware, and no number is cited for it here pending a bench descriptor dump. A configuration-gated hardware load switch (using real USB configured state, not VBUS presence) is recorded as a future compliant-host option, with no part or firmware mechanism chosen.

## Physical header numbering

J20/J30 are the left 20-contact strips: carrier contact `k` corresponds to Pico position `k` (1–20). J21/J31 are the right strips: contact `k` corresponds to Pico position `41-k` (40 down to 21). This convention is recorded explicitly in `design/circuit.json` and checked in the data tests.

J20/J21 accept Pico H. J30/J31 accept the display module. Do not merge these two 40-position interfaces electrically. Only the documented LCD signals, select signals, ground and intended power path pass through the carrier.

## G01 — do not route a presumed power connection

The present netlist proposes display Pico-position 39 (VSYS) fed by fused 5 V, with positions 36 (3V3), 37 (3V3_EN), 35 (ADC_VREF) and 40 (VBUS) isolated. **This is conditional and not power-qualified.** The module schematic was readable as extracted text, but its power-strapping diagram could not be visually verified in this environment. Verify the exact received module revision, its regulator/strap resistors and required GPIO level supplies before finalizing the header footprint/netlist.

The Waveshare board can have extra memory/clock/power-control nets on otherwise spare Pico positions. GP3, GP5 and GP14 on the display header are not automatically tied to the custom carrier's mux controls or timing output. Trace any additional requirements from the correct manufacturer schematic. Do not energize an unverified arrangement and assume a blank screen is a firmware issue.

The independent source files are listed in `catalog/sources.json`. `scripts/fetch_sources.py --execute` downloads available originals locally; retrieval does not establish that they have been reviewed.

## Signal contract

| Function | Pico GPIO |
|---|---|
| HOLD, LINK | GP0, GP1; active-low buttons |
| Mux address bit 0…3 | GP2, GP3, GP4, GP5 |
| Mux disable | GP7; HIGH disconnects all banks |
| LCD DC / CS | GP8 / GP9 |
| SPI1 SCK / MOSI / MISO | GP10 / GP11 / GP12 |
| LCD backlight / reset | GP13 / GP15 |
| Timing test point | GP14 |
| Touch / SD deselect | GP16 / GP22 |
| Signal / TIME / RANGE ADC | GP26 / GP27 / GP28 |

All address changes occur while mux disable is high in the diagnostic firmware. LCD backlight has a pull-down, chip-selects pull high. Do not assume asynchronous analog and digital 3.3 V startup is harmless: qualify power sequencing and unpowered injection into the mux/ADC paths.

## Provisional power allocation

Allocate 300 mA to the screen/backlight module, 80 mA to Pico and 40 mA to carrier analog/control circuitry for planning. These are **budget allowances, not measured or manufacturer maximum currents**. Their sum is 420 mA; verify USB startup/enumeration limits, F1 derating, local capacitance and connector ratings. At 40 mA the analog LDO's ideal 5-to-3.3 V dissipation is about 68 mW, excluding any abnormal condition. Do not infer a thermal pass from this estimate.

Structured module-power evidence (module VSYS capacitance, backlight topology, and the disputed 180 mA claim) lives in `design/evidence/module-power.json`, one status (`verified-schematic` / `allowance` / `unknown` / `rejected`) per claim, consumed by `scripts/power_budget.py` and this page so they cannot disagree. The module's own VSYS capacitors total a verified 11.2 µF; combined with carrier C30 (1 µF) that is a known 12.2 µF carrier+module nominal subtotal, reported against the informal ≤10 µF inrush guidance -- not a claim of measured inrush compliance, since Pico-side bulk capacitance is still unknown. The backlight is a CAT1 regulator feeding LED-A, with three LED cathode returns to ground through R17-R19; CAT1's identity and output current remain unknown. F1 sits between `VBUS_USB` and `+5V_FUSED` and carries only the display+analog branch (340 mA), not the full 420 mA total source current: at a 1.5x sizing margin that is a 510 mA target, 10 mA above the selected `1206L050YR` candidate's 500 mA nominal hold rating, with no manufacturer temperature-derating curve retained to confirm its actual derated hold current. A PPTC is not a precision USB current limiter. See `reports/power-budget.json`'s `f1_branch_sizing` and `downstream_capacitance_5v_fused` sections for the full figures.


`design/power-contract.json` also holds the declared USB configuration-descriptor value that `scripts/power_budget.py` checks the 420 mA allowance against. That declared value is currently 250 mA -- the unmodified Pico SDK 2.1.1 default, not a project override: the pinned SDK source does not guard `USBD_MAX_POWER_MA` with `#ifndef`, so a compile-time override does not reliably change the compiled descriptor, and no unverified hand-written descriptor replacement is shipped without a hardware bench to check it against (see `power-contract.json`'s `override_investigation`). Because 420 mA exceeds that declared 250 mA, `reports/power-budget.json`'s `usb_budget.vs_declared_limit` correctly reports `fail`, not a masked pass -- this module currently declares less configured power than its own planning allowance, on top of already requiring a source outside the ordinary staged USB budget (see "USB source contract" above).

## G01/G06 pending decision — backlight default-on conflict (not applied)

Desk evidence (#3) found that the display module's own R16 (10k, VSYS -> LCD_BL) pulls the backlight-enable/CAT1-EN node toward the module's ~5 V VSYS rail. Against the carrier's R88 (100k, LCD_BL -> GND), and with GP13 left high-impedance until firmware drives it, the node sits near 4.5 V: the backlight defaults **ON**, not off (the carrier pull-down does not give an off default), and 4.5 V is above the RP2040 GPIO absolute maximum of IOVDD + 0.5 V (small clamp current, estimated below 0.1 mA, unmeasured). This appears to be the vendor's own stacked behaviour, not a carrier design error.

This is recorded as a **pending G01/G06 proposal only** (`pending_g01_changes` in `design/circuit.json`, id `g01-r88-backlight-default`): no component value is changed here, and R88's value/net is unchanged in the generator. The local G01 procedure (issue #16's `LOCAL-HANDOFF.md`) decides, after the physical module check, whether to keep R88, remove it, or accept and document the default-on behaviour.

Citations: Waveshare Pico-ResTouch-LCD-3.5 schematic p1, LCD BACKLIGHT (3A), R16 10K VSYS->LCD_BL/CAT1 EN; RP2040 datasheet Sec 5.5.3.1, Table 622 (PDF p615).

architecture/acquisition.title: Acquisition, bandwidth and memory
architecture/acquisition.body:
## Three independent mux outputs

U7 selects one of ten buffered signal channels into ADC0. U8 selects one of ten TIME controls into ADC1. U9 selects one of ten RANGE controls into ADC2. They share four address bits and a disable signal, but their analog common outputs are never connected together.

Each mux common output is buffered by its own TLV9064 section, followed by 100 Ω / 1 nF at the corresponding ADC pin. The mux switches already-conditioned unipolar signals, never raw ±12 V inputs. The precise settling time at 3.3 V, charge injection, crosstalk, and ADC acquisition after a large step must be measured.

## Intended later high-rate schedule

The [Pico SDK ADC documentation](https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/pico-sdk/hardware.html) specifies 500 ksample/s aggregate and 12-bit conversion, but only about 8.7 effective bits for RP2040. Ten channels do not each get that aggregate rate. Address switching, ADC input switching, settling, firmware overhead and display servicing also consume time.

P0 reserves a 100 µs frame: ten 8 µs signal slots (80 µs), two 8 µs control slots (16 µs), and 4 µs margin. A slot is intended to disable/change/enable the mux, settle, discard one ADC conversion, and retain a second conversion. Each frame reads TIME and RANGE for one advancing control channel, giving a nominal 1 kHz control scan per channel. Every signal would receive one sample/frame, or 10 ksample/s.

This is a **timing design target**, not an implemented 100 µs real-time engine. The delivered Pico diagnostic intentionally runs much slower and reports raw codes over USB. Develop the high-rate timer/DMA/PIO or tightly bounded acquisition engine only after measuring real settling. Reserve hardware timer timestamps and record overruns instead of silently claiming a rate.

Maximum nominal signal-channel skew is 72 µs between the first and tenth slots. “Ten signals visible” is not simultaneous sampling. LINK TIME changes viewing windows, not sample timing. Phase or transient comparisons require correction for known channel offsets and an explicit common trigger model.

## Memory and display

A whole 320 × 480 RGB565 framebuffer is 307,200 bytes. It does not fit in RP2040's 264 kB SRAM. Do not allocate it and hope compression or the linker fixes the problem.

Use streamed strips or tiles; for example a 160 × 16 RGB565 tile is 5,120 bytes, or 10,240 bytes double-buffered. The portable history implementation uses 77,800 bytes for ten channels: ten levels × 192 min/max bins, retaining both extrema through decimation. At 10 ksample/s the coarsest 512-sample bins span about 9.83 seconds, sufficient for the proposed 8.192-second window. Min/max is an envelope representation: do not label those extrema as uniformly resampled raw points.

At 8 MHz, a full RGB565 payload alone takes 307.2 ms; at 24 MHz it takes 102.4 ms. Commands, software and bridge behavior add overhead. P0 starts at 8 MHz. Update only necessary tile regions, reduce redraw rate gracefully, and prioritize acquisition. Never infer 30 FPS full-screen performance from a vendor maximum SPI clock.

## Accuracy and clipping

Nominal input-referred ADC code width is about 8.07 mV using 3.3 V / 4096. This is a scale factor, not effective measurement resolution or absolute accuracy. Op-amp/reference error, source impedance, ADC nonlinearity and noise require characterization. UI should show a clear UNCAL indicator until calibration is installed. Display one or two decimals conservatively; do not make an unjustified three-decimal voltmeter.

Distinguish VIEW CLIP (signal exceeds ±3/5/8 pane scale) from ADC SAT (conversion near an ADC rail). A ±8 V display does not certify ±8 V tolerance or prove absence of an overload outside the sampled instant.

architecture/controls-and-ui.title: Physical controls and display behavior
architecture/controls-and-ui.body:
## Time and range

TIME is a dedicated 10 kΩ linear ALPS pot for each channel. Its electrical reading maps exponentially from a 2 ms whole-pane window to 8.192 seconds: `T = 0.002 × 4096^(code/4095)`. Endpoint calibration, averaging and a deadband are required to prevent jitter. Keep the physical knob position meaningful; do not turn it into an endless menu encoder.

RANGE is an actual maintained three-position SP3T switch. The selected NKK SS14MDP2 has On-On-On behavior, not a two-position SPDT and not a centre-OFF toggle. Throws select ground, a shared 1.65 V resistor midpoint and analog 3.3 V. The common feeds its own 1 kΩ / 100 nF filter and the RANGE mux. The draft uses logical C/L/M/H terminal labels until its numeric pin map is obtained.

Software decodes low, middle and high bands as ±3, ±5 and ±8 V. Deadbands retain the previous setting; a valid new setting must persist for 20 ms. This avoids intermediate readings during break-before-make travel. Filtering and software debouncing do not qualify the contact material at its actual low current.

HOLD freezes the plots; acquisition continues. LINK makes CH1's TIME control the source for all panes. Turning LINK off immediately restores the ten actual pot positions; it does not overwrite them. Both are press-to-toggle buttons with 20 ms debounce, and small on-screen labels indicate the active mode. LINK is a time-link of views, not phase synchronisation: all channels are still sampled sequentially.

## Screen layout

The firmware renderer (`firmware/src/scope_render.c`, details in `firmware/LCD-BACKEND.md`) draws ten 160 × 96 logical-pixel panes on the 320 × 480 portrait screen, two columns of five. Numbering is column-major, to preserve the physical banks: left controls 01–05 correspond to the five left-column panes, top to bottom, and right controls 06–10 to the right column, so CH6 is top right. Do not interleave screen labels 01/02 on the first row while the controls use a different order. The simulator follows this assignment, and `scripts/validate_extra.py` checks the firmware, simulator and panel study against each other.

Each pane has, from top to bottom:

- a label row: the two-digit channel ID in the channel colour, the vertical scale the plot is drawn at (`±3V` / `±5V` / `±8V`), `UNCAL` while the channel has no installed calibration, and the window duration, right-aligned (`2.0ms` … `8.19s`);
- a 4-pixel channel colour tag beside a 144 × 66 waveform plot, with the zero line and the newest sample at the right;
- a status row: the signal token `VIEW CLIP` or `ADC SAT`, then `LINK` and `HOLD` while those modes are latched;
- a one-pixel separator.

Text uses a 5 × 7 clean-room font on a 6 × 10 cell grid and is redrawn only when it changes. At the manufacturer's pixel pitch each complete pane is about 24.48 × 14.69 mm. This is a compact visual monitor, not ten large DATA-sized screens. Check the simulator at physical scale and print the panel SVG at 100% before committing the screen size.

## TIME mapping on screen

Each pane spans the whole window chosen by its TIME knob (or CH1's under LINK): W = round(`0.002 × 4096^(code/4095)` s × 10,000 samples/s), from 20 samples (2 ms) to 81,920 samples (8.192 s). The renderer draws it from the smallest min/max history level whose 192 bins cover W, so the existing ten levels reach 8.192 s with no extra memory. Columns merge bins (keeping each column's minimum and maximum, so an extreme anywhere in the window stays visible) or repeat them when there are fewer bins than columns. Each edge of the represented interval is within one coarse bin of the requested window: at most 512 samples, 51.2 ms, at the longest windows. With partial history the retained data sits right-aligned and the not-yet-recorded time stays blank. The duration label and the plot come from the same W, so the label names the interval the plot represents.

## RANGE mapping and calibration

The ±3/±5/±8 V ranges are software view scales: the switch does not change the analog path. Each column's raw minimum and maximum codes are converted to volts through that channel's calibration, then ±range maps to the plot height: +range at the top row, 0 V on the zero line, −range 64 rows lower, symmetric about zero. The zero line is electrical zero through the same mapping, not a fixed mid-scale code. With the nominal transfer, a +3 V input reaches the top edge at ±3 V and 3/8 of the positive half-height at ±8 V.

Until a calibration is installed the renderer uses an explicit nominal fallback, the ideal front-end figures in `reports/analog-analysis.json` (zero code 1858.378, about 8.07 mV/code), and the pane shows `UNCAL`. No calibration-persistence mechanism exists yet (`firmware/tools/calibrate.py` only writes a host JSON file), so every pane currently shows `UNCAL`. Nothing auto-zeroes at startup, and no per-channel calibration data is assumed. `scripts/validate_extra.py` checks the firmware's nominal constants against the analysis report.

A deadband reading keeps the last valid scale. Before the switch has ever decoded, the plot uses ±8 V and the scale label shows it in the warning colour. The scale label always names the scale the plot is drawn at, so under HOLD it stays with the frozen plot.

Two distinct conditions are reported in the status row. `VIEW CLIP` means converted volts exceed ±range: the trace is pinned at the edge with a separate warning-coloured marker, and only the view clips. `ADC SAT` means a raw code of 0 or 4095 in the drawn window, an ADC or input limit; it comes from raw codes, not volts, and takes priority. A clipped ±3 V view never reads as an ADC limit. Neither indicator certifies ±8 V tolerance or proves the absence of an overload between samples. All of this is host-tested against a pixel model; on-screen behaviour on the physical module is still an open G06 item.

## Simulator limits

`doc/public/prototype/index.html` is a synthetic interaction prototype: it generates mathematical waves in the browser. It demonstrates pane layout, clipping, controls, hold and linked time, not measured acquisition fidelity, display refresh performance, hardware noise, multiplexed skew or electrical protection.

No touch feature is used even though the selected purchased module has a touch overlay. A future lower-cost non-touch module can be substituted only after its exact electrical and mechanical interfaces are reviewed.

how-to/firmware.title: Firmware handoff
how-to/firmware.body:
## Delivered and tested

`firmware/src/scope_core.c` is portable C for ADC-to-voltage conversion, measured two-point calibration, logarithmic TIME mapping, RANGE decoding with debounce, and bounded multiresolution min/max history. `python3 scripts/test_firmware.py` compiles and runs it on the host with warnings treated as errors. These tests exercise mathematics and data handling; they do not prove RP2040 operation.

`firmware/src/pico_diagnostic.c` initializes the specified pins, scans the three mux outputs with conservative delays, and writes raw CSV values over USB serial. It deliberately leaves the LCD off and does not implement the ten-channel high-rate engine. No prebuilt UF2 is supplied because target compilation and hardware execution were unavailable.

## Local target build

Install a reviewed Pico SDK and an ARM compiler in your usual local toolchain. Set `PICO_SDK_PATH` to the checkout. The package does not run an unpinned SDK download during CMake configure.

```sh
cmake -S firmware -B firmware/build -DPICO_BOARD=pico
cmake --build firmware/build
```

The above builds only `scope10_diagnostic`, after local source/toolchain review. Record compiler/SDK versions and build hashes. Do not flash/energize the assembled module interface before G01 power/pin checks.

## LCD integration remains open

Download the vendor example archive from the source manifest. Its module uses an SPI-to-parallel bridge around ILI9488; this is not necessarily the same transfer framing as a raw ILI9488 SPI panel. Adapt the exact 3.5-inch vendor driver to the GPIO table and disable touch/SD access. Confirm reset, CS, DC, RGB565 byte order, orientation, address-window writes and backlight behavior using color bars and corner markers before waveform drawing.

`display_port.h` specifies the renderer's small-rectangle API. There is intentionally no no-op fake backend: an application using these calls cannot link until a real implementation is supplied. Do not allocate a 307,200-byte framebuffer or use a generic driver with an assumed RGB666 pixel protocol.

## Calibration and data provenance

`firmware/tools/calibrate.py measured.csv calibration.json` requires two measured DC points for every channel. Input columns are `channel,volts,mean_code`. Use the actual DMM-measured fixture voltage; do not pass an assumed front-panel generator setting as ground truth. Inspect intermediate 0, ±3, ±5 and ±8 V residuals after fitting. Store board serial, date, fixture identity, temperature, firmware hash and source CSV with the calibration file.

Persistent flash storage, CRC/versioning, safe defaults, a real-time display renderer, trigger alignment, DMA/PIO acquisition and hardware tests are not complete. They have explicit acceptance tasks rather than success claims. Never perform automatic “zero at startup” on attached signals.

how-to/kicad.title: KiCad completion procedure
how-to/kicad.body:
## What opens locally

Start with `hardware/kicad/zudo-scope10-p0.kicad_pro`. The root schematic links ten child sheets: power, module interfaces, acquisition, five dual-input pages and two control pages. All selected pin mappings and values come from `design/circuit.json`, generated by `scripts/make_design.py`. There are 224 physical instances in the draft and 134 named nets.

The symbols are intentionally pin-complete rectangular review symbols. They are not polished conventional circuit drawings. The text netlist and `design/connections.csv` provide an independent review surface. Global labels carry inter-sheet connections. The host checks compare generated pin/net memberships; they are not native KiCad ERC.

The `.kicad_pcb` is **only a 250 × 180 mm rectangular outline**, with no footprints or tracks. Do not manufacture it. Mechanical mounting holes listed in the requirements are proposals and are not drilled in that outline.

## Required work before placement

1. Reacquire and visually review the exact display schematic/CAD and NKK switch drawing. Resolve all physical pin identities, including duplicated PJ-313 terminals.
2. Select actual MPNs and supplier codes for resistors, capacitors, fuse and four module-header strips. The passive resistor tolerances, voltage ratings and capacitor dielectrics are constraints, not interchangeable generic labels.
3. Verify every symbol pin to actual footprint pad. The locally supplied XUNPU footprint is drawing-derived, not independently approved. Generic SOIC/TSSOP/SOT package names are candidates, not evidence of exact footprint correctness.
4. Confirm the Pico and display socket heights, component face, mirrored row numbering, module service clearance, USB access and control panel stack. Exact display hole/connector geometry is still unavailable here.
5. Open all generated files in the current KiCad, fix any native format issues, save, run ERC and reconcile every electrical finding with the source specification. Preserve project-generated evidence and report native tool/version/results.

## Routing guidance

Use a continuous low-impedance ground reference under signal and digital circuits; do not automatically split the ground plane and force return currents across gaps. Separate the LCD/SPI and backlight return paths spatially from biased input nodes and reference distribution. Place each amplifier's 100 nF bypass at its supply pins. Keep the 1 MΩ / 200 kΩ / 249 kΩ high-impedance node compact and clean, with the clamp and first capacitor close to the input amplifier.

Keep the mux-common traces short; place the three post-mux buffers and ADC RC networks near their loads. Treat display clock, address edges and source-series resistors as a coupled noise/settling problem. Run representative worst-case pattern tests with the display active as well as dark.

The four-layer, 1.6 mm board is a starting point for grounding and routing convenience, not a paid fabrication stackup. Confirm assembler-supported layer/copper/thickness options and actual mechanical constraints before locking it. A later compact or two-layer cost-down is a separate layout qualification.

## Release sequence

After native ERC, placement and routing, refill planes and run DRC, schematic-to-PCB parity, pin-map checks and mechanical review. Export Gerbers, drill, assembly BOM, CPL and STEP only from that reviewed revision. Review JLC's placement rendering and obtain written assembly acceptance for every fitted line. Archive the exact exported bytes and checksums. `manufacturing/release_guard.py` blocks release while any gate remains open; it does not replace engineering review.

how-to/procurement.title: Sourcing and no-home-soldering contract
how-to/procurement.body:
## Factory scope

Deliver the custom carrier with every fitted electrical item soldered: all passives, six op amps, three muxes, reference/regulator, ten jacks, ten pots, ten range switches, two buttons and all four module connector strips. No “hand-fit after delivery” connector, wire link or programming header is acceptable.

Supply a genuine preheadered Pico H and an assembled Waveshare SKU 19907. Either the assembler integrates them, or the user plugs the tested modules into already-populated sockets while unpowered. Nut tightening, cap fitting, standoffs and plugging a finished harness are mechanical assembly, not soldering. A socketed module does not mean untested electrical assembly is acceptable.

[JLCPCB's assembly capabilities](https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-assembly-capabilities) describe mixed through-hole and surface-mount routes. [Global sourcing](https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/how-to-use-jlcpcb-global-sourcing-parts-service) and [consignment](https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/how-to-consign-parts-to-jlcpcb) are procurement routes, not approval of this part/board combination. Do not ship supplier parts to an assembler before obtaining receiving and assembly instructions.

## Current sourcing gaps

The catalogue identifies TLV9064IDR/C388176, 74HC4067PW,118/C179326, TLV75533PDBVR/C404027, BAV199/C40919, the ALPS pot, XUNPU button and SHOU HAN jack. Recheck stock and tiers at quotation. NKK SS14MDP2/C6684954 was listed with zero stock: select pre-order/global sourcing or an approved external supply. Its numerical terminal map remains open. Separately, SS14MDP2 is a silver-contact part used in this design's near-zero-current dry sense circuit; the manufacturer's own dry-circuit guidance recommends gold contacts for that regime, so it is `OPEN_REQUIRES_MANUFACTURER_CONFIRMATION_AND_QUALIFICATION` (catalogue record `range`; see `design/evidence/range-contact.md`) rather than sourcing-approved for this application, independent of the stock question.

REF3330AIDBZR is an exact proposed MPN, but no JLC assembly availability was established. Resistor/capacitor records deliberately include unselected supplier identities rather than invented C-numbers. The Pico sockets, display headers, fuse, knob caps, spacers and mounting screws also need exact mechanical/orderable selection.

## Cost honesty

A single display eliminates nine screens and their interconnects, but does not make ten dedicated knobs and range controls free. The selected Waveshare page showed $19.99 for the module on 2026-09-26; it excludes Pico, carrier, controls, assembly, shipping and taxes. NKK switches may dominate the control budget. Obtain the prototype quote before assuming this is a sub-$30 assembled monitor.

For quotation compare three separate figures: populated carrier; preassembled external modules; mechanical finishing/functional test. Separate non-recurring assembly/fixture charges from per-board costs and calculate at the intended prototype quantity. `manufacturing/cost-template.json` leaves unknown prices null so they cannot disappear into an apparently complete total.

The most promising later cost reductions are qualifying an inexpensive exact SP3T switch, integrating RP2040 onto the board, qualifying a bare non-touch LCD, reducing panel/PCB area, and relaxing dedicated control count only with the user's explicit agreement. P0 does not silently replace the ten controls with a shared menu.

how-to/qualification.title: Bring-up and acceptance matrix
how-to/qualification.body:
## Before the populated board is powered

Ask the assembler or bench-service provider to check component identity, numeric pin mapping, solder joints, shorts, module orientation, power/header continuity and the exact approved module revision. Confirm F1 and USB source current path. Use a current-limited 5 V source and keep the display backlight disabled initially. Rework belongs to that provider, not the home workstation.

Power tests first establish analog/digital rails, 3.0 V reference, startup/off decay, USB current and absence of back-power. Measure current separately with no display, dark display and bright display. Obtain board/module thermal images or measured hot-spot temperatures under worst intended load.

## Channel tests

Use a verified low-voltage signal fixture with the same ground and appropriate current limits. Begin with inputs shorted to ground, then step through measured ±1, ±3, ±5, ±8 and ±12 V. Record raw codes and DMM readings for all ten channels. Verify expected open-input bias rather than treating it as a defect or auto-zeroing it away. Test all TIME endpoints/direction and all three RANGE positions.

After normal-range DC validation, check 1 Hz, 10 Hz, 100 Hz, 500 Hz and 1 kHz signals, then deliberately characterize aliasing above the intended range. Compare displayed amplitude against reference instrumentation and the predicted filter transfer function. Distinguish source distortion from this monitor's filtering, conversion and display effects.

Worst-case mux test: alternate a near-positive-full-scale channel and a near-negative-full-scale channel, hold neighboring channels at zero, and measure residual settling/crosstalk with the LCD off and active. Increase rate only while recording discarded/kept conversion timing and overrun counts. An 8 µs slot is acceptable only when its measured error meets the reviewed target.

## Separate abnormal-voltage qualification

Do not apply ±24 V merely because the design spreadsheet contains it. First review all clamp paths and absolute maximum constraints, then conduct a controlled powered/unpowered current-limited test at a suitably equipped provider. Inspect both source and internal node currents and any back-powered rail. ESD immunity is a separate test; successful DC injection is not an IEC ESD claim.

## Initial proposed acceptance limits

These are engineering targets, not achieved results. Review them after the first measured sample:

| Item | Proposed target |
|---|---|
| Calibrated DC residual, low-impedance source | no more than 100 mV over ±8 V, excluding noise outliers |
| Channel crosstalk on DC steps | no more than 100 mV input-referred after the selected settling interval |
| Reliable useful bandwidth | characterize DC–1 kHz amplitude error; do not assume flatness |
| High-rate acquisition | ten actual 10 ksample/s streams with counted overruns and measured skew |
| RANGE state | stable reading after 20 ms; no indefinite intermediate-state oscillation |
| LCD behavior | all ten panes, correct orientation/colors/labels; readable physical-scale text |
| User assembly | no unsoldered electrical part or wire after delivery |

No hardware result is prefilled in `manufacturing/acceptance-results.csv`. Failed items remain visible. The first populated prototype may require a second PCB revision; do not shift that rework onto the user.

how-to/documentation.title: Local zudo-doc integration
how-to/documentation.body:
## Two usable reading paths

The offline catalogue and simulator need only Python's local HTTP server. The `doc/` source also targets the native zudo-doc framework used by the lamp project: one config, package-owned route stubs and MDX content. It is not a clone of the lamp's full component validation framework.

The lamp's key principle is retained: **structured component data are authoritative; pages are a generated projection**. Edit `catalog/components.json`, source records or narrative inputs, then run `python3 scripts/build_docs.py`. Do not edit the generated component pages independently.

## Official scaffold route

The included `scripts/bootstrap_doc.sh NEW_DIRECTORY` invokes the published `create-zudo-doc@5.27.0` scaffold in an empty directory, copies this package's MDX, public assets and minimal config into it, and leaves dependency installation to you. It does not modify your existing lamp project or a pre-existing target directory.

```sh
bash scripts/bootstrap_doc.sh /path/to/new/scope-doc
cd /path/to/new/scope-doc
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm dev
```

The framework package/build tool were not installed or built in this environment because network package downloads were unavailable. Native build and interaction checks remain local tasks; the separate offline site is already generated.

For an existing zudo-doc workspace copy `doc/src/content/docs/`, `doc/public/` and the selected configuration fields, resolving category collisions deliberately. Keep public source binaries under review: manufacturer files are retained for local engineering reference and do not automatically carry permission for unrestricted republication.

## Component evidence

Each generated record carries exact or unresolved identity, role, package candidate, pin mapping, source links, retained file hashes, source availability and separate open questions. A verified part identity does not mean a verified footprint, a verified factory process, an assembled board or a successful measurement. Blank asset sections say explicitly that a model or datasheet was not recovered.

The pot has an original downloaded manufacturer STEP and drawing files recovered from the earlier component ZIP. The Pico/display STEP files were not downloaded successfully; the mechanical envelope study is not substituted for exact CAD. Missing binary downloads are listed and a local source-fetch script is supplied.

architecture/mechanical.title: Panel and mechanical study
architecture/mechanical.body:
## Concept layout

The 250 × 180 mm panel study puts the portrait screen at the centre, five TIME/RANGE pairs on each side, and the ten input jacks at the outside edges. Left screen column 01–05 matches the left control bank; right column 06–10 matches the right bank. HOLD/LINK sit below the display. Jacks face outward so cables do not lie across the screen.

The SVG has real millimetre dimensions but is an **ergonomic study, not a fabrication drawing**. The screen active rectangle uses the manufacturer's stated 48.96 × 73.44 mm portrait area. Its exact placement within the module/window and its connector/bushing stack must be verified from the received module/CAD. Socket height, standoff height, underside Pico clearance and USB service access remain open.

`mechanical/envelope-study.scad` and its exported files describe a nominal slab and control/module envelopes only. They do not include exact terminal geometry or validated mounting holes. They must never be mistaken for a board STEP exported from a routed, populated KiCad design.

Use `reference/assets/pot/RK09L1140-F15.STEP` for the actual ALPS pot geometry; retain its manufacturer provenance. Do not infer pot rotation/offset relative to a footprint merely because its STEP renders correctly.

## Mechanical release checklist

Check shaft length above the final panel, cap and finger spacing, panel thickness, switch lever reach, button access and retention. Use the chosen pot nuts and load-bearing supports rather than leaving all user forces on solder joints. Check plug insertion force, TS plug sleeve/ring behavior, cable bend radius and no live circuitry touching a conductive panel.

Confirm the display and Pico may be unplugged only unpowered and cannot be shifted by one header pin during assembly. Bare unkeyed strip headers do not prevent reversed or offset insertion; specify visible pin-1 markings, mechanical alignment and an inspection procedure or choose keyed connectors for production. No drilling or exact enclosure machining should precede this review.
